reading.body:
The World of AI's data infrastructure map includes a facility tagged as a data center in Dueville, Italy, but cannot confirm its operator, capacity, or company identity from available sources.

OpenStreetMap identifies a telecoms facility near Vicenza in the Veneto region as "Set," a name too generic to establish what company operates it or what function it serves beyond the data-center tag itself. The Veneto region does host technology businesses and light industry, making a small data center plausible in the area, but the available record cannot confirm this. No operator website, power capacity, or Italian business registration could be located before research resources were exhausted.

This entry represents a hard constraint on mapping AI infrastructure: facilities exist in public records with names so minimal or obscured that their operators remain unknown. For tracking compute availability and power demand, a data center without confirmed capacity data or operator contributes location information only. It does not reveal whether this facility serves AI workloads, what its power draw is, or whether it adds to or subtracts from grid strain in northern Italy.

The Padova airfield lies 21.6 miles away, the nearest airport in the record. Beyond geography, this facility illustrates how incomplete data persists in infrastructure mapping, and why compute availability at regional scale remains difficult to measure with precision.
